method: Introduces 'hidden dependence' for random vectors and proves that small probability-distance perturbations of a reference joint law (marginals fixed) attain the same unconstrained worst-case bounds for gamma-tail risk measures; illustrates with a stylised credit-loan portfolio.
reason: All numerics are analytic illustrations on assumed homogeneous credit portfolios (n=500 or 50,000, p=0.01, rho=0.10) with a Gaussian reference copula. No dataset of any kind is used, so there is nothing measured on real market data to replicate.

method: Characterises the full set of increasing profits (a strong arbitrage) in a one-dimensional general-diffusion market with a constant-rate bank account, in terms of an auxiliary signed measure nu and a canonical strategy theta built from the scale function and speed measure.
reason: Entirely a mathematical-finance proof paper: no tables, no figures, no data. Nothing empirical to reproduce.

method: Crosses four deep forecasting backbones (TimesNet, DLinear, N-BEATS, iTransformer) with three output heads (point/Huber, single-Gaussian NLL, K=4 Gaussian-mixture NLL) on S&P 500 monthly log-returns 1871-2023, under 5 anchored walk-forward folds x 3 seeds, scoring CRPS-skill, pinball, coverage, Diebold-Mariano and Model Confidence Set, plus ARIMA(2,0)/GARCH(1,1) classical baselines.
reason: The target series is a long monthly S&P 500 return history, freely available from the Shiller ie_data CSV and, for the post-1927 portion, from Yahoo ^GSPC; the cross-asset panels are ordinary listed tickers. Everything else is model code with fully specified hyperparameters (d_hidden=64, K=4, initial train fraction 0.50 = 916 months, test window 128 months, step 183 months, seeds 0/1/2), so the head-vs-backbone gradient is directly rerunnable.
data_needed: S&P 500 monthly log-returns 1871-01 to 2023-12 (about 1,832 months) - Shiller ie_data free CSV; post-1927 cross-check with Yahoo ^GSPC monthly closes
Cross-asset / cross-frequency generalisation panels (equity index and daily-frequency series) - Yahoo Finance daily and monthly closes
Risk-free rate if an excess-return variant is wanted - FRED DGS3MO or Ken French RF
reproducible_targets: Head-mean CRPS-Skill-Score vs TimesNet_point: point head -0.09% (spread 0.78%), Gaussian head +1.18% (spread 5.07%), GMM head +3.59% (spread 4.61%)
Head gradient point-to-GMM = 3.7 percentage points; point-to-Gaussian about +1.3% CRPS, Gaussian-to-mixture a further about +2.4%
Model Confidence Set on squared errors excludes none of the 12 variants at the 5% level
GARCH_gmm is the best h=1 model at +12.92% CRPS-SS and best h=3 at +10.33%, then collapses to -50.52% at h=6; N-BEATS_gmm at h=6 is +55pp better than GARCH_gmm

method: CLQT is a closed-loop LLM portfolio-manager benchmark: agents run a five-stage gather/synthesize/allocate/execute/reflect cycle over 26 bi-weekly rounds under a hard TimeGate, institutional cost model, three-tier memory and an MCP tool layer, scored on a five-axis APM-CS capability scorecard, with a module ablation grid and a live broker track on post-cutoff data.
reason: The headline validation is a live broker track on 18 NYSE days (2026-06-15 onward) that is unseen post-cutoff by construction, so rerunning it later cannot reproduce it. The backtest track additionally depends on a multi-provider news/sentiment channel registry and on stochastic LLM rollouts whose per-round allocations are not published as a fixed series, so the Sharpe and scorecard numbers are not recoverable from free price data alone.

method: Trains a physics-informed DeepONet (hard-constrained ansatz plus residual-based adaptive refinement) to learn the Heston pricing operator across the whole six-parameter space, benchmarked against the semi-analytic Heston solution and a finite-difference solver, and diagnoses noise in the ATM Greeks.
reason: Training requires no labelled data at all - the loss is the Heston PDE residual on sampled collocation points - and every reported accuracy figure (final training loss 1e-5, price and Greek errors) is measured against a synthetic semi-analytic benchmark. No market option prices are used anywhere.

method: Formulates adaptive AI delegation as a Governance-Aware POMDP with Bayesian belief updating and a Belief-at-Risk penalty, then validates it with synthetic stress tests, confidence-only perturbations, forecast-accuracy sweeps, governance-appetite sensitivity, fragile-AI early warning, and a benchmark against five governance heuristics.
reason: Every reported number is generated from simulated AI-quality regimes (low-reliability, noisy, improving, high-reliability) with cached or perturbed AI confidence streams; the 'historical market replay' is only a backdrop for those synthetic AI evidence streams, which are not published. There is no empirical claim about market data that free prices could reproduce.

method: Derives the variance-optimal (Galtchouk-Kunita-Watanabe) hedge for claims on forward curves driven by an HJMM SPDE with infinite-rank stochastic covariance, proving density of finite-maturity and delivery-window strategies, convergence of finite-rank spectral projections, and an exact bucket/rank/residual decomposition of the quadratic hedging error.
reason: Illustrations are analytic examples in affine stochastic-covariance, multiplicative HJMM and CIR stochastic-covariance models. No dataset, no market forward curves, nothing empirical.

method: Trains deep-hedging RL agents under MSE, downside-risk and CVaR objectives to hedge swaptions with one, two or three hedging swaps, benchmarked against sensitivity-based rho-hedging, with SHAP attribution of hedge weights, a KAN-vs-FCNN comparison, and misspecification stress on the kappa and theta parameters.
reason: All experiments run on paths simulated from a three-factor arbitrage-free dynamic Nelson-Siegel model; the hedging-error distributions and every performance metric are Monte-Carlo outputs, not measurements on real swaption or swap quotes. Historical swaption surfaces would in any case be vendor-only.

method: Builds collective and individual actuarial risk models whose claim processes are driven by an underlying stochastic (SIS epidemic) population with interacting subpopulations, derives scaling limits, and provides bounds and approximations for ruin probabilities.
reason: Purely theoretical, with Monte-Carlo illustrations of the ruin-probability bounds under assumed parameters (T=1000, F0 in {0.2, 0.7}). No dataset, and the subject is insurer solvency rather than traded markets.

method: Introduces a regime-adaptive KS / GL-KS self-similarity test built on the discrete Grunwald-Letnikov fractional derivative, proves the filtered empirical-process limit and consistency of the resulting Hurst estimator, validates by Monte Carlo, then applies it to daily log-realized-volatility series and to daily equity-index log-price trajectories to detect rough volatility and persistent / anti-persistent / efficient market states.

The realized-volatility half needs an intraday-derived RV series, which is the weaker link, but the log-price Hurst table stands on its own.
data_needed: Daily closes for the index panel - Yahoo tickers ^AEX, ^AORD, ^AXJO, ^BFX, ^BVSP, ^DJI, ^FCHI, ^FTSE, FTSEMIB.MI, ^GDAXI plus the remaining realized-library indices, full history to about 2023 (sample lengths 5,900 to 13,500 daily observations)

Monte Carlo fBm/fGn paths at H in {0.1,...,0.9} and N in {100, 250, 500, 1000, 5000} for the size, power and RMSE tables
reproducible_targets: Indices where the unfiltered KS branch is selected: AXJO 0.4921 (0.4684-0.5159), BVSP 0.4875 (0.4631-0.5120), FCHI 0.4964 (0.4747-0.5181)

method: Builds a Bayesian pipeline with three arms: a discount-factor dynamic linear model (delta=0.98, beta=0.98) for one-step-ahead log-realized volatility and 95% VaR on daily S&P 500 returns (train 2000-2019, out-of-sample 2020-01-02 to 2024-12-30, T=1,257), Bayesian logistic regression for card-fraud detection on IEEE-CIS, and a hierarchical Beta state-space model for compliance risk, benchmarked against GARCH(1,1)-t and a two-layer LSTM.

method: Prices American options and flexible-forward FX contracts under a time-inhomogeneous Heston model via a recursive matrix-Riccati characteristic function and a Volterra early-exercise integral equation, solved with a double-COS expansion and a damped-Sinc local-basis scheme, benchmarked against a penalty-iteration MCS-ADI finite-difference solver.

method: Multi-method event study of two Japanese bank M&A events - the 2005-10-03 MUFG creation and the 2018-04-01 Resona Holdings merger - estimating cumulative abnormal returns with the market model, CAPM and Fama-French three-factor model over roughly a -20 to +22 day window, then VAR Granger-causality tests and impulse responses for spillovers to peer banks, plus propensity-score matching for the ATT.

Event dates, windows and models are published, so the CARs and t-statistics are directly recomputable.

method: Studies a Stackelberg game in which one reinsurer sets a common premium and an investment strategy while many heterogeneous insurers choose retention and investment under relative-performance concerns; characterises follower equilibrium retention by a scalar fixed point, proves a threshold structure from full cession to full retention, reduces the leader problem to one dimension, and establishes finite-player to mean-field convergence.
reason: A game-theoretic paper whose figures are equilibrium maps and convergence plots computed from assumed parameter values (h=1 and h=2.3 heterogeneity cases). No dataset at all, and the domain is reinsurance pricing rather than traded markets.

method: Benchmarks six pretrained time-series foundation models run zero-shot (TimeGPT, TimeGPT-LH, TimesFM-2.5, Moirai-2.0, Chronos, Chronos-2) against five train-from-scratch neural baselines (NBEATS, NHITS, PatchTST, iTransformer, KAN) on daily linear and log returns of five liquid U.S. equities (AAPL, AMZN, GOOG, JPM, META), under an equalized context budget L=512, a rolling-origin protocol with 20-business-day forecast windows, scored by rMAE against a zero-return random walk and one-sided Diebold-Mariano tests.
reason: The entire dataset is daily adjusted closes of five mega-cap U.S. tickers, free from Yahoo Finance, and the protocol (context length, horizon, rolling origin, random-walk benchmark, rMAE) is fully specified in a reproducibility record table. The pretrained models are all publicly downloadable checkpoints run zero-shot, so no proprietary input is required.
data_needed: Daily adjusted closes for AAPL, AMZN, GOOG, JPM, META - Yahoo Finance, enough history to supply an L=512 context plus rolling-origin evaluation folds
Both linear returns (P_t/P_{t-1} - 1) and log returns for the 10 tasks (5 assets x 2 return representations)

method: Introduces amortizing perpetual options (AmPOs), where implicit installment payments are replaced by decay of the claimable notional to preserve fungibility, shows the valuation reduces to a vanilla perpetual American option on a dividend-paying asset, and derives closed-form exercise boundaries, prices, Greeks and comparative statics in the amortization rate.
reason: A contract-design and derivation paper. The two figures are illustrative comparative-statics examples (an at-the-money call comparison and the vega of a $100 straddle position) computed from assumed parameters. No dataset is used.

method: Decomposes a portfolio's squared price-of-risk premium (an integrated conditional squared Sharpe functional) into intervention-stable premium, a signed confounding wedge and a nonnegative information loss, shows the decomposition is well posed exactly under filtration immersion, and constructs a minimal order-three obstruction invisible to every singleton and pairwise admissibility screen.
reason: The abstract states the experiments run on synthetic single- and multi-driver panels (K=5 drivers, L=3 confounders, planted triples), and every figure is a recovery or screening diagnostic on those simulated panels. No real prices or drivers are used.

method: Builds scale- and fluctuation-dependent correlation matrices from the multifractal detrended cross-correlation coefficient rho_r, compares their spectra to synthetic Gaussian and q-Gaussian references, and applies the framework to one-minute returns of 140 major cryptocurrencies over 2021-2024 to extract a dominant market mode and sectoral components and to check that the filtered bulk matches the random-matrix limit.
reason: The empirical claim is measured on one-minute intraday returns for 140 coins across four years, roughly 2 million bars per asset. None of the permitted free sources supplies that: Yahoo crypto history is daily and Coinbase spot candle history is depth-limited and does not cover a 140-coin cross-section at minute frequency. The result is scale-dependent by construction, so a daily-frequency substitute would not land on the same eigenvalue spectra.

method: Forecasts the U.S. and euro-area zero-coupon term structure (3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y, weekly, U.S. April 1987 to February 2025 and Europe backcast to February 1992) with classical models (dynamic Nelson-Siegel, PCA, AFNS) and neural networks that either forecast factors or forecast zero rates directly, adding macro features raw or compressed by an autoencoder, and evaluates with RMSE, MAE, directional accuracy plus a duration-managed bond trading strategy.
reason: Every input is free: U.S. zero rates are FRED/U.S. Treasury constant-maturity series, euro-area triple-A zero rates come from the ECB Data Portal (from September 2004), the German proxy curve used to backcast to 1992 is free from the Bundesbank, and all macro series are FRED and Eurostat/ECB. The paper cites Thomson Reuters DataStream only as a convenience alongside FRED. Model architectures, DNS lambda=0.0606 and autoencoder shapes (7-3-7 and 7-5-3-5-7) are specified.
data_needed: U.S. zero rates at 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y, weekly, April 1987 to February 2025 - FRED DGS3MO, DGS6MO, DGS1, DGS2, DGS3, DGS5, DGS10 (or the U.S. Treasury par-yield-curve feed)
Euro-area government AAA zero-coupon spot rates for the same maturities, September 2004 to February 2025 - ECB Data Portal yield-curve series
German government zero rates February 1992 to February 2025 for the backcast proxy (3M from Oct 2005, 6M from Nov 1997, 1Y from Feb 1994, 2Y/3Y/5Y/10Y whole period) - Bundesbank time-series database
U.S. macro series (Table 4) and German/euro-area macro series (Table 5) - FRED and Eurostat/ECB

method: Defines a robust hedging valuation adjustment as the worst-case expected loss over a relative-entropy ball around the simulated loss distribution of a no-trade-band delta-hedging rule for a one-year at-the-money European call (252 steps, 20,000 Monte Carlo paths), then calibrates the benchmark stress level from public data by computing rolling Kendall rank correlation between the VIX and the SPY Amihud illiquidity measure and mapping it to a Gaussian scale.
reason: The simulation machinery is synthetic, but the calibration of the benchmark stress level is a genuine empirical claim measured on real market data and both inputs are free: CBOE VIX from FRED and daily SPY prices and volumes (Stooq in the paper, identically available from Yahoo). The rolling-window rule (756 trading days, stepped every 21 days, first window 2005-02-28 to 2008-02-28, last ending 2026-01-09), the Amihud formula and the tau-to-rho map are all published, so the reported stress percentiles are directly recomputable. Confidence is moderate because only this calibration layer, not the HVA tables, rests on real data.
data_needed: CBOE VIX daily close, 2005-02-28 to 2026-01-09 - FRED series VIXCLS (or Yahoo ^VIX)
SPY daily close and volume over the same span for the Amihud measure ILLIQ_t = |r_t| / (P_t * volume_t) - Yahoo Finance SPY (paper used Stooq)

Rolling-window rule: 756 trading days stepped every 21 trading days, Kendall tau between VIX and SPY Amihud per window, mapped by rho_pub = sin(pi*tau/2) and floored at zero; a 126-day window variant for the sensitivity table
reproducible_targets: In high-stress windows (top decile of average VIX), the 90th percentile of rho_pub_wwr is about 0.364 and the 95th percentile about 0.368 under the 756-day rolling rule, which is what motivates the rounded benchmark stress level rho_0 = 0.40

Fixed-radius interpretation drifts away from 0.40 as the band widens: high-liquidity b=0.5 gives rho_eq 0.317 and eps_req/eps_fixed 1.54; medium-liquidity b=0.5 gives 0.263 and 2.29; low-liquidity b=0.3 gives 0.208 and 3.03

method: Models Uniswap v3 concentrated-liquidity AMMs as networks of priced timed automata suitable for UPPAAL and as tick-level finite-state transducers specifiable in TLA+, encoding the piecewise constant-product invariant, fee-growth variables and tick-crossing rules, and proves that a tick-wise invariant is preserved up to an explicit rounding bound.
reason: A formal-methods paper: contributions are automata encodings, TLA+ instances and rounding-error theorems, verified by model checking rather than against pool data. No on-chain dataset is analysed, and no empirical claim on market data is made.

method: Compares a passive equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolio of 30 U.S.-listed commodity ETFs (2018-12-12 to 2024-12-16, daily) against rolling-window mean-variance and CVaR(95%/99%) optimized portfolios, long-only and restricted long-short, at both the minimum-risk and tangent points, then repeats the exercise dynamically with ARMA-GARCH marginals and a Student-t copula, and adds Hill tail-index and VaR/CVaR extreme-value diagnostics.

The optimization criteria, rolling-window design and metrics are all specified.

method: Presents a linear-algebra method that prices Bachelier-type options and computes Greeks for infinitely many strikes within a convergence range from only a finite number of expectations, derives an explicit convergence range for SABR, and illustrates on SABR and rough Bergomi.
reason: A pure numerical-analysis paper with no tables, no figures and no data in the digest; all examples are model-generated under assumed SABR and rough Bergomi parameters. Nothing empirical to reproduce.

method: Introduces a dynamic Bayesian network framework (MMHC, PC-Stable and SI-HITON-PC structure learning) for 10-day 99% VaR and stressed VaR, using both historical and forecasted returns, and compares it against ARCH(1), GARCH(1,1), EGARCH(1,1), RiskMetrics (each under normal and skewed Student-t innovations), historical simulation and delta-normal, on daily S&P 500 log returns from 15 March 1991 to 14 February 2020 with 7,286 rolling forecasts per model, evaluated by breach counts and forecasting error measures.
reason: The only dataset is daily S&P 500 index closes over 1991-2020, free from Yahoo ^GSPC, and every competing model is a standard, fully specified estimator. Breach counts, breach dates and error measures are all published, and even the DBN structure-learning algorithms are open-source (bnlearn), so this is a clean end-to-end replication.
